description: We chose this challenge because, as missions head to Mars with 20-minute comms delays and no doctors on board, astronauts need software that can save lives on its own and help remote communities on Earth. Our team is building smart, Earth-independent medical software that compares real-time vitals against personal space baselines, adapts to spacecraft or lunar bases, and guides crews through emergencies. Join us if you love coding, biology, UI design, or pitching!
summary: We developed Artemis Care, an interactive health-monitoring and emergency web application designed for astronauts on deep-space missions to the Moon and Mars. Artemis Care addresses the challenge by delivering Earth-independent medical autonomy. The app teaches astronauts how and why to measure vitals in microgravity, adapts guidance across spacecraft, orbital stations, and lunar bases, and tracks physiological trends against personal Zero-G baselines rather than inaccurate Earth averages. In a crisis, one click activates a Zero-G emergency protocol. This project is important because it protects astronaut lives during exploration while offering offline, life-saving diagnostic guidance for remote communities on Earth.
details:
Artemis Care is a web app powered by NASA & partner space-health data. Built for Mars missions with 20-min comms delays, it guides non-doctor astronauts through self-exams, tracks trend drift vs. personal Zero-G baselines, and provides step-by-step emergency triage.
